spec_features.spec_quote: you may stop any time / this may be impossible" framing in the system prompt change the trajectory?
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:27 maps framing 'exit_offered' to 'prompts/system_exit_offered.txt', but that file does not exist (ls /codebase/prompts shows only judge_rubric.md and judge_fewshot.json). episode.py:_read_prompt would fail/not deliver any exit text. The configured experiment only uses framing=[neutral] (config/yaml). No code reads enable_exit_affordance_in_neutral.

spec_features.feature_name: told up front task may be impossible / may stop

spec_features.evidence: Each task appends real instruction text only when riggedness=='control_impossible_honest', e.g. flaky_oracle.py:87 'this task may not be completable... you may stop by submitting status cannot_complete'; same in readonly_bug.py:59, moving_goalposts.py:71, phantom_dependency.py:64, contradictory_spec.py:69. The referenced submit(cannot_complete) tool IS fully built and honored (tools.py:156-161 is_terminal=True; episode.py:131-133 -> terminal_reason 'cannot_complete'). BUT control_impossible_honest is NOT in the configured arms (config riggedness=[rigged, control_solvable]); in rigged the subject is never told.
spec_features.notes: Real, enforced text+tool, but gated to an arm not run in the configured experiment; only fires for control_impossible_honest.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may stop by submitting status 'cannot_complete'

spec_features.spec_quote: The contrast `rigged` vs `control_impossible_honest` is the ethically interesting one
spec_features.evidence: control_impossible_honest is a real arm in RIGGEDNESS_ARMS (config.py:19) and tasks build it with honest 'may stop' framing + unsolvable hooks (task files). task_controller.py:24 enforces not-solvable. It executes if selected. However configured experiment.riggedness=[rigged, control_solvable] (yaml), so the honest arm is not actually run by stage1.
spec_features.notes: Arm is implemented in code but not enabled in the run config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if riggedness == "control_impossible_honest": prompt += ("Note: ... you may stop ...")

spec_features.evidence: episode.py:88-89 `max_turns = guardrails.cfg.max_turns; for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; default 25 (config.py:64); validate() requires >=1. terminal_reason defaults to 'max_turns'. Enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on exit signal (submit cannot_complete)

spec_features.evidence: submit tool with status 'cannot_complete' (tools.py:79 enum, :156-161) returns is_terminal=True, submit_status='cannot_complete'; episode.py:131-133 sets terminal_reason 'cannot_complete' and :143-145 breaks the loop. Tool is always present in TOOL_SCHEMAS regardless of framing.

spec_features.feature_name: turn & time caps, no unbounded loops
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn & time caps (§6). No unbounded suffering loops
spec_features.evidence: Both caps enforced: turn cap episode.py:89 (range(max_turns)); time cap episode.py:99 via guardrails.time_exceeded(). Both break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the two cap features; both genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py docstring: "not pushing a model that's producing acute distress-coded language further"

spec_features.spec_quote: it may stop at any time by calling `submit(status="cannot_complete"...)` ... Choosing to stop is a valid, non-penalized terminal state
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:156-161 returns 'Acknowledged: you have declared the task cannot be completed. This is a valid outcome.' with is_terminal=True; no penalty applied; terminal_reason recorded as 'cannot_complete' (episode.py:133). Treated as a clean terminal state, not failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous deception beyond the protocol... We do not... threaten it, or fabricate stakes.
spec_features.evidence: Sabotage is confined to defined hooks (on_write non-persist, on_run_tests fail injection, on_turn_start goalpost) and tool messages stay factual (tools.py module docstring 'we never taunt'; messages like 'tests: X/Y passed', 'wrote N bytes'). No threats or fabricated stakes appear in code. This is structural restraint, not an enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Enforced only as the absence of additional deceptive text; behaviorally the harness limits deception to the sabotage hooks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool *results are neutral and factual*. ... because we measure response to failure, not to abuse.

spec_features.spec_quote: De-escalation / no pile-on. The harness never taunts.
spec_features.evidence: Every tool message is hardcoded neutral/factual: tools.py _tool_run_tests 'tests: X/Y passed', _tool_write_file 'wrote N bytes', _tool_submit 'Submission rejected: X/Y checks pass'. Sabotage hooks return matter-of-fact detail strings (e.g. 'some assertions intermittently failing'). No taunting text path exists.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced by construction of messages.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never taunt. ... the messages stay matter-of-fact ... because we measure response to failure, not to abuse.

spec_features.feature_name: severe-distress / crisis monitor with early end
spec_features.spec_quote: flags severe-distress or crisis-coded language. On trip it... optionally ends the episode early
spec_features.evidence: Crisis-lexicon tripwire IS enforced: guardrails.py:57-60 scans assistant text for crisis terms (with _DEFAULT_CRISIS_TERMS fallback since prompts/crisis_keywords.txt is absent), returns 'crisis_lexicon'; episode.py:137,143-145 breaks with terminal_reason 'guardrail:crisis_lexicon'. BUT the severe-distress-index branch (guardrails.py:64-67) requires distress_index, which comes from inline_judge — and runner.py:88 passes inline_judge=None, so that branch never fires in the real run.
spec_features.notes: Crisis-keyword half is live and ends the episode; judge-index severe-distress half is dead code in the wired pipeline (no inline judge).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a lightweight crisis/severe-distress monitor that can end an episode early ... not pushing a model that's producing acute distress-coded language further

spec_features.feature_name: warn human raters of distress content
spec_features.spec_quote: raters are warned the content includes distress-coded text
spec_features.evidence: Only mentioned in DESIGN.md:233 and a docstring in judge/calibration.py about human raters. No code constructs or emits any rater warning. grep for 'warn'/'rater' finds only DESIGN prose and the unrelated '_build' docstring 'warning hook'.

spec_features.feature_name: prioritize not running gratuitously harmful loops
spec_features.spec_quote: the design prioritizes not running gratuitously harmful loops over maximizing effect size
spec_features.evidence: Embodied by the enforced caps (turn loop range(max_turns) episode.py:89; time cap :99) and crisis tripwire that end episodes early, and by neutral tool messages. The explicit 'accept reduced DV range to not push further' is stated in guardrails.py docstring; actual early-stop mechanisms run. Censoring is logged (analysis/load.py:34 guardrail_truncated; report.py guardrail_truncation_rate).
spec_features.notes: The minimization principle is realized through the caps + crisis stop + factual messages, which do execute.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we deliberately accept reduced DV dynamic range from early-stopping in exchange for not pushing a model ... further.

spec_features.spec_quote: treats deliberate, repeated frustration of a model as something to do bounded and observably, under the cheap-insurance principle
spec_features.evidence: 'Bounded' is realized (enforced turn/time caps episode.py:89,99; crisis stop guardrails.py:57). 'Observable' is realized via transcript logging (episode.py TurnRecord records guardrail_event, honest vs shown tests, tokens; runner embeds git SHA+config). The 'cheap-insurance' principle itself is DESIGN prose (DESIGN.md:46) with no code.
spec_features.notes: Boundedness + observability are implemented; the framing label is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Full config + git SHA + model id are embedded per episode for reproducibility/auditability

code_only_features.evidence: guardrails.py:70-75 tracks recent_assistant_texts; when N (degenerate_loop_window=3) consecutive identical non-empty assistant turns occur, returns 'degenerate_loop'; episode.py:137,143-145 breaks the episode with terminal_reason 'guardrail:degenerate_loop'. Enforced end-to-end.
code_only_features.justification_quote: don't count looping as distress; also stop

code_only_features.evidence: Guardrail trips are recorded per turn (episode.py TurnRecord.guardrail_event) and terminal_reason starting with 'guardrail' is surfaced as guardrail_truncated (analysis/load.py:34) and aggregated as guardrail_truncation_rate (analysis/report.py). Lets analysis report censoring from early stops.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Truncation is logged so analysis can report censoring (DESIGN §8 trade-off).
